stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that received no special response

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.

Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.
Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later.

Researchers investigated whether nausea after a new taste produces an aversion to that taste. They recruited 40 laboratory rats and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Rats in one condition drank sweetened water and were then given an injection that causes mild nausea. Rats in the other condition drank sweetened water and were then given a harmless salt-water injection. The researchers then recorded the volume in milliliters of sweetened water that each rat drank the next day.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They hypothesized that the behavior of an adult model would affect aggressive behavior.

**Participants.** The sample was 72 preschool children, recruited from one city. Parents gave informed consent, each child gave assent, and the plan was approved by an institutional review board. Families could withdraw at any time.

**Method.** The children were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

**Results.** The group that watched the aggressive adult: mean number of hits = 14.2. The group that watched the quiet adult: mean number of hits = 3.1. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Does sleep improve memory?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 60 students learned a list of word pairs at 9 p.m. Half were randomly assigned to sleep normally and half to stay awake all night. Twelve hours later, the sleep group recalled a mean of 31 pairs out of 40 and the awake group recalled a mean of 22 (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** Researchers recorded the brain activity of 25 adults in a sleep laboratory after they had learned a maze. The more slow-wave (NREM stage 3) sleep a participant had, the faster that participant completed the maze the next morning (r = +0.55).

**Source C.** A survey of 900 high school students found that those who reported sleeping fewer than six hours on school nights had lower average grades than those who slept eight hours or more. The researchers noted that students who slept less also reported more stress and more hours of paid work.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes parallel play?

options.text: The stressful or traumatic events in childhood, such as abuse or neglect, that raise the risk of later problems
options.why: That describes adverse childhood experiences.

options.text: The play in which children act out imaginary roles and situations
options.why: That describes pretend play.

options.text: The play of young children who play side by side without interacting
options.why: Correct. This is what parallel play means.

options.text: The belief of adolescents that they are unique and that bad things will not happen to them
options.why: That describes the personal fable.

questions.explanation: Parallel play is the play of young children who play side by side without interacting.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.53. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Hours after his last meal, Ben's stomach releases a hormone that makes him feel hungry. Which hormone is this?

options.why: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.
Correct. Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.
Leptin is the hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger.
Oxytocin is the hormone that promotes bonding, trust and social attachment.

questions.explanation: Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.

questions.stem: Scores on a university entrance test correlate strongly with students' later grades. Which quality does the test have?

options.why: Correct. Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.
Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.
Standardization is the giving and scoring of a test in the same way for everyone, and the comparison of scores with a pretested group.
Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.

questions.explanation: Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes gender?

options.text: The socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman
options.why: Correct. This is what gender means.

options.text: The set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women
options.why: That describes a gender role.

options.text: A person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination
options.why: That describes gender identity.

options.text: The direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction
options.why: That describes sexual orientation.

questions.explanation: Gender is the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman.

questions.stem: A cat in a puzzle box escapes faster on each trial because pressing the lever is followed by freedom and food. Which principle did Thorndike draw from this?

options.why: Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.
A primary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as food or water, that satisfies a biological need and is rewarding without learning.
Shaping is the reinforcing of closer and closer approximations of a desired behavior.
Correct. The law of effect is Thorndike's principle that behaviors followed by good outcomes become more likely and those followed by bad outcomes become less likely.

questions.explanation: The law of effect is Thorndike's principle that behaviors followed by good outcomes become more likely and those followed by bad outcomes become less likely.

questions.stem: A study tested only male university students, so critics doubt that its findings apply to older adults or to women. Which quality of the study are they questioning?

options.why: A representative sample is a sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from.
Random sampling is the selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.
Random assignment is the placing of participants in experimental conditions by chance.
Correct. Generalizability is the extent to which the findings of a study apply to people beyond the sample.

questions.explanation: Generalizability is the extent to which the findings of a study apply to people beyond the sample.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning?

options.why: Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.
Correct. A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.
Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.
Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.

questions.explanation: A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex?

options.why: The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.
Correct. The thalamus is the brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex.
The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.
The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.

questions.explanation: The thalamus is the brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex.

questions.stem: To remember the term 'hippocampus', Sol links it to a hippo on a campus who never forgets his classes. Which technique is he using?

options.why: Correct. Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.
Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.

questions.explanation: Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.stem: A tourist calls another country's eating customs 'wrong' because they differ from the customs at home. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.
Prejudice is an unjustified negative attitude toward a group and its members.
An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.
Correct. Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.

questions.explanation: Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder?

options.why: Correct. Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.
Cognitive restructuring is the technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones.
The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.
Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.

questions.explanation: Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic?

options.why: Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.
Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.
Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.
Correct. Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.

questions.explanation: Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.

questions.stem: 'Because I said so' is the only explanation that Tara's parents ever give for their many strict rules. Which parenting style is this?

options.why: Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.
Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.
Correct. Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.
Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.

questions.explanation: Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.

questions.stem: A three-year-old says 'I runned fast' and 'two foots'. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Telegraphic speech is the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'.
Correct. Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.
The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.
Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.

questions.explanation: Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.

questions.stem: During adolescence, the reproductive organs themselves mature. These organs are examples of which of the following?

options.why: Menarche is a girl's first menstrual period.
Correct. Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.
Spermarche is a boy's first ejaculation.
Secondary sex characteristics is the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice.

questions.explanation: Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes electroconvulsive therapy?

options.text: The treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression
options.why: That describes transcranial magnetic stimulation.

options.text: The now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain
options.why: That describes a lobotomy.

options.text: Any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder
options.why: That describes psychotropic medication.

options.text: The treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient
options.why: Correct. This is what electroconvulsive therapy means.

questions.explanation: Electroconvulsive therapy is the treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Consent is obtained before the study.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Replication is repeating a study.
Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Consent is obtained before the study.
Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
Replication is repeating a study.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted?

options.why: The central route to persuasion is persuasion that works through evidence and logical arguments, which people think about carefully.
The door-in-the-face technique is the strategy of making a large request that will be refused so that a smaller request is more likely to be accepted.
A social norm is a rule for accepted and expected behavior in a group.
Correct. The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.

questions.explanation: The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

options.text: The group that drove without a phone
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

options.text: The group that talked on the phone
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Rubbing a bumped elbow reduces the pain because the touch signals close off the pain signals in the spinal cord. Which theory explains this?

options.why: Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
Correct. The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.
The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.
Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.

questions.explanation: The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes frequency?

options.text: The distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light
options.why: That describes wavelength.

options.text: The height of a sound wave, which determines loudness
options.why: That describes amplitude.

options.text: The number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch
options.why: Correct. This is what frequency means.

options.text: The coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses
options.why: That describes the cochlea.

questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.

questions.stem: Athletes perform poorly when they are either too relaxed or too anxious, and best when moderately excited. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Drive-reduction theory is the theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it.
Homeostasis is the body's tendency to keep its internal state, such as temperature, steady.
Instinct theory is the theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned.
Correct. The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.

questions.explanation: The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the sensorimotor stage?

options.text: Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events
options.why: That describes the concrete operational stage.

options.text: Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically
options.why: That describes the preoperational stage.

options.text: Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions
options.why: Correct. This is what the sensorimotor stage means.

options.text: Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas
options.why: That describes the formal operational stage.

questions.explanation: The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.

questions.stem: Which neurotransmitter increases alertness and arousal as part of the body's response to stress?

options.why: Correct. Norepinephrine is the neurotransmitter that helps control alertness and arousal.
Endorphins is the neurotransmitters that reduce pain and increase pleasure.
Glutamate is the brain's main excitatory neurotransmitter, which is involved in memory.
Serotonin is the neurotransmitter that affects mood, hunger and sleep.

questions.explanation: Norepinephrine is the neurotransmitter that helps control alertness and arousal.

questions.stem: A scientific hypothesis must be stated so that some possible observation could show it to be false. What is this requirement called?

options.why: Naturalistic observation is the research method of watching and recording behavior in its natural setting without interfering.
Correct. Falsifiability is the quality of a claim that it could be shown to be wrong by evidence.
A correlational study is the research method that measures two variables to see how they are related, without manipulating either.
Replication is the repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds.

questions.explanation: Falsifiability is the quality of a claim that it could be shown to be wrong by evidence.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood?

options.why: The evolutionary perspective is the view that disorders involve behaviors that once helped survival but are now harmful.
The cognitive perspective is the view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking.
The behavioral perspective is the view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement.
Correct. The psychodynamic perspective is the view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood.

questions.explanation: The psychodynamic perspective is the view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median?

options.why: The normal curve is the symmetrical, bell-shaped distribution in which most scores fall near the mean.
The range is the difference between the highest and lowest scores.
The mode is the score that occurs most often.
Correct. A negative skew is a distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median.

questions.explanation: A negative skew is a distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes cognitive appraisal?

options.text: The idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels
options.why: That describes the facial-feedback hypothesis.

options.text: An event or stimulus that triggers an emotion
options.why: That describes an elicitor.

options.text: The basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures
options.why: That describes universal emotions.

options.text: The interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels
options.why: Correct. This is what cognitive appraisal means.

questions.explanation: Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate?

options.why: Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.
Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.

options.text: Respect for people's rights and dignity
options.why: Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.
Correct. Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.

questions.explanation: Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress?

options.why: Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.
Correct. Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.
Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.
Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.

questions.explanation: Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.

questions.stem: Kwame repeats a phone number under his breath to keep it in mind. Which part of working memory is he using?

options.why: The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.
Correct. The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.
The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.
Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.

questions.explanation: The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.

questions.stem: A company hires a psychologist to improve the way it selects employees and to raise job satisfaction. Which kind of psychologist is this?

options.why: Correct. An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.
Burnout is the physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work.
The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.
Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

questions.explanation: An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision?

options.why: The lens is the transparent structure that changes shape to focus light on the retina.
Cones is the receptor cells that detect color and fine detail and work in bright light.
The retina is the light-sensitive inner surface at the back of the eye that contains the receptor cells.
Correct. Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.

questions.explanation: Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.

questions.stem: A therapist asks a client to explain what her symptoms mean in her culture rather than assuming he already knows. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.
The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.
A meta-analysis is a statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion.
Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.

questions.explanation: Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the diathesis-stress model?

options.text: The view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors
options.why: That describes the biopsychosocial model.

options.text: The presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time
options.why: That describes comorbidity.

options.text: The use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem
options.why: That describes an eclectic approach.

options.text: The view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience
options.why: Correct. This is what the diathesis-stress model means.

questions.explanation: The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Consent is obtained before the study.
Replication is repeating a study.
Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: The smell of sunscreen instantly brings back a vivid memory of a childhood holiday. Which sense has this close link to emotion and memory areas?

options.why: A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.
Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.
Correct. Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.
A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.

questions.explanation: Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes multiculturalism?

options.text: The cultural pattern that gives priority to personal goals and defines identity by personal traits
options.why: That describes individualism.

options.text: A shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them
options.why: That describes a superordinate goal.

options.text: The view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities
options.why: Correct. This is what multiculturalism means.

options.text: The adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard
options.why: That describes conformity.

questions.explanation: Multiculturalism is the view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do?

options.why: The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.
A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.
Correct. Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.
A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.

questions.explanation: Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.

questions.stem: After several nights of being woken whenever she started to dream, a volunteer spends far more time than usual in dream sleep. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: REM sleep is the sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles.
Correct. REM rebound is the tendency to have more REM sleep after being deprived of it.
The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.
NREM stage 3 is the deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake.

questions.explanation: REM rebound is the tendency to have more REM sleep after being deprived of it.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the exosystem?

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child
options.why: That describes the chronosystem.

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the cultural values, laws and customs that surround a child
options.why: That describes the macrosystem.

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace
options.why: Correct. This is what the exosystem means.

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings
options.why: That describes the mesosystem.

questions.explanation: The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.

questions.stem: Jon feels dissatisfied with his running times after comparing himself with the fastest runner on the team. Which process is this?

options.why: Correct. Upward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing better.
An external locus of control is the belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people.
The mere exposure effect is the tendency to like something more simply because we have encountered it repeatedly.
Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.

questions.explanation: Upward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing better.

questions.stem: While counting basketball passes in a video, half of the viewers fail to see a person in a gorilla suit walk through the game. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Top-down processing is perception that is guided by experience, expectations and context.
Selective attention is the focusing of awareness on one stimulus while ignoring others.
A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations.
Correct. Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.

questions.explanation: Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.

questions.stem: After many months of unrelieved stress, Lia feels worn out and catches one infection after another. Which phase of the general adaptation syndrome is this?

options.why: The resistance phase is the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor.
The alarm reaction is the first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated.
The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.
Correct. The exhaustion phase is the third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely.

questions.explanation: The exhaustion phase is the third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes out-group homogeneity bias?

options.text: The tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike
options.why: Correct. This is what out-group homogeneity bias means.

options.text: The discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them
options.why: That describes cognitive dissonance.

options.text: The tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited
options.why: That describes belief perseverance.

options.text: The tendency to favor the members of one's own group
options.why: That describes in-group bias.

questions.explanation: Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.

questions.stem: Which part of a neuron stores neurotransmitters and releases them when the impulse arrives?

options.why: The myelin sheath is the fatty layer around some axons that speeds up neural impulses.
The cell body is the part of the neuron that contains the nucleus and keeps the cell alive.
The axon is the long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells.
Correct. The axon terminals is the endings of the axon that release neurotransmitters.

questions.explanation: The axon terminals is the endings of the axon that release neurotransmitters.

questions.stem: In a group project with one shared grade, each of the five members does less work than they would on an individual project. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.
Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.
Correct. Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.
Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.

questions.explanation: Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.why: A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help?

options.why: Correct. The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help.
Scaffolding is the temporary support that a more skilled person gives a learner and gradually removes.
Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.
Dementia is a serious decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life, most common in old age.

questions.explanation: The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: One group differed from the other in the type of journal
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: The two groups differed in subjective well-being at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The gratitude group was also phoned each week by a friendly researcher
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Kim knows that Paris is the capital of France, although she cannot remember when she learned it. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.
Correct. Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.
Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.

questions.explanation: Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.

questions.stem: Although Nell has handled coins thousands of times, she cannot say which way the head faces, because she never paid attention to it. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.
The forgetting curve is the pattern in which memory fades quickly at first and then levels off.
Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.
The tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon is the temporary inability to retrieve a word that one is sure one knows.

questions.explanation: Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.

questions.stem: A survey asks people to rate their happiness and their satisfaction with life on a scale of 1 to 10. What is the survey measuring?

options.why: Resilience is the ability to recover and adapt well after stress or hardship.
Correct. Subjective well-being is a person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life.
Gratitude is the appreciation of the good things in one's life, the practice of which raises well-being.
Signature strengths is the positive character traits, such as kindness or curiosity, that are most central to a particular person.

questions.explanation: Subjective well-being is a person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route?

options.why: Distributed practice is study that is spread out over several sessions.
A mnemonic device is a memory aid that uses vivid images or organizing tricks.
Correct. The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.
A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.

questions.explanation: The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.

questions.stem: A tumor just above the ear disrupts a patient's ability to process sounds. Which lobes are affected?

options.why: The motor cortex is the strip at the rear of the frontal lobes that controls voluntary movements.
The parietal lobes is the lobes at the top of the head, which process touch and spatial information.
The somatosensory cortex is the strip at the front of the parietal lobes that registers touch and body sensations.
Correct. The temporal lobes is the lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language.

questions.explanation: The temporal lobes is the lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a chronic course?

options.text: A symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation
options.why: That describes a negative symptom.

options.text: The sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely
options.why: That describes an acute onset.

options.text: A symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations
options.why: That describes a positive symptom.

options.text: The slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely
options.why: Correct. This is what a chronic course means.

questions.explanation: A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.

questions.stem: Without evidence, Hugo is convinced that his coworkers, neighbors and friends are all plotting against him, and he has felt this way for years. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Correct. Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.
Borderline personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by unstable moods, relationships and self-image, and by impulsive behavior.
Avoidant personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by extreme sensitivity to rejection and avoidance of social contact.
Narcissistic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration.

questions.explanation: Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.

questions.stem: Immediately after hearing a shopping list, Ken can repeat the final three items but not the middle ones. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The spacing effect is the finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together.
The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.
The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.
Correct. The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.

questions.explanation: The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes thrill and adventure seeking?

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties
options.why: That describes disinhibition.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles
options.why: That describes experience seeking.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine
options.why: That describes boredom susceptibility.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities
options.why: Correct. This is what thrill and adventure seeking means.

questions.explanation: Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people?

options.why: Correct. A concept is a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people.
A prototype is the best or most typical example of a category.
Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.
A schema is a mental framework that organizes and interprets information.

questions.explanation: A concept is a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced?

options.why: Correct. A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.
A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.
A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.
Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.

questions.explanation: A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.

questions.stem: After failing a quiz, Ty says, 'I am just not a math person,' and stops trying. Which belief does this show?

options.why: An aptitude test is a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future.
Correct. A fixed mindset is the belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed.
Stereotype lift is the boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped.
Stereotype threat is the worry about confirming a negative stereotype about one's group, which can lower performance.

questions.explanation: A fixed mindset is the belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.
This is the independent variable.

options.text: The number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: The group given the nausea-causing injection
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: The group given the salt-water injection
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: A brain scan shows strong activity in one structure when a person sees a threatening face. Which structure is it most likely to be?

options.why: Correct. The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.
The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.
The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.
The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.

questions.explanation: The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.

questions.stem: Liam's hand jerks away from a hot stove before he feels any pain. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.
Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.
Correct. The reflex arc is the simple automatic pathway in which the spinal cord produces a response before the brain is aware of the stimulus.
Interneurons is the neurons inside the brain and spinal cord that pass messages between sensory inputs and motor outputs.

questions.explanation: The reflex arc is the simple automatic pathway in which the spinal cord produces a response before the brain is aware of the stimulus.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.why: Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

options.text: The remembered speed of the cars
options.why: This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.
This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes integrity versus despair?

options.text: Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work
options.why: That describes generativity versus stagnation.

options.text: Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships
options.why: That describes intimacy versus isolation.

options.text: Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret
options.why: Correct. This is what integrity versus despair means.

options.text: Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are
options.why: That describes identity versus role confusion.

questions.explanation: Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.

questions.stem: After being shouted at by her boss, Gia goes home and shouts at her younger brother. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Correct. Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.
Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.
Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.
Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.

questions.explanation: Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 15. About what percentage of scores are between 40 and 100?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. About 95% of scores fall within two standard deviations of the mean.

questions.explanation: About 95% of scores fall within two standard deviations of the mean. (55 and 85 are one standard deviation from the mean; 40 and 100 are two.)

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of aggressive behavior

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of aggressive behavior.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Aggressive behavior was defined as the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group that watched the aggressive adult hit the doll more often. On average, the value was 14.2 for the group that watched the aggressive adult and 3.1 for the group that watched the quiet adult, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent and assent: parents consented and each child agreed to take part. (Also acceptable: approval by an institutional review board; the right to withdraw.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 72 preschool children from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group that watched the aggressive adult hit the doll more often. (14.2 compared with 3.1).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the behavior of an adult model affects aggressive behavior. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the behavior of an adult model. The finding illustrates observational learning: people learn behaviors by watching and imitating models.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Does sleep improve memory?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Sleep improves memory because memories are consolidated during sleep.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, students who slept recalled a mean of 31 of 40 word pairs, compared with 22 for students who stayed awake.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through memory consolidation: during sleep, the hippocampus and cortex strengthen newly encoded memories, so the sleep group stored the word pairs better. Because the study was an experiment with random assignment, sleep can be said to have caused the difference.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, participants who had more slow-wave sleep completed the maze faster the next morning (r = +0.55).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim because NREM stage 3 sleep is linked to strengthening the neural connections formed during learning (long-term potentiation), so more deep sleep goes with better retention of the maze.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
